class_guess: Bell eats counter, two-level: a down-counting binary zone (bits 3 cells apart, anchored at the far end) bitten from its low end; W4-2's architecture mirrored
summary: Wall walks the bell, counting a zone down; bites its low end each cycle. Halts only if an overflow hits q=4.
mechanism: R(p,q,Z) = 0^inf (10)^p 1 C> 0 0 (10)^q Z: each round the wall 00 moves 2 pairs right (q-2) and the zone Z counts down by 1 (zeros = set bits on the lattice j = w-1-3i); at v = 0 it refills (O0/O1/O2). At q <= 2 the wall bites Z's low end (B0/B1/B2/B2') and a new cycle starts with n one or two pairs longer.

Two levels: per two calm cycles v drops by 1; near n = 2^(L+1) the zone gains a bit (level-up), sometimes through a chaotic phase of nested bites (B2'', closed as a stack of the same rules in Wave 5). The closed rules reproduce the direct run at all 4,197 cycle starts to 1e11.

Why it never halts (Wave 5): the invariant I = {d = n - 2^(cap+1) >= 2, M = n + 2v - 2^(cap+2) != 0 mod 3}. Every rule keeps M or negates it mod 3, and the only halting starts from d >= 2 have M = 0. The blank run is in I from step 327. Checked on 7.9M states; two sub-lemmas (continuation cycles, nested levels) still need a paper argument.

history.skeleton: 0^inf C> 0 0 (10)^n Z 0^inf  (cycle start R(-1,n,Z); Z has width w, counter value v, L bits)

rules.name: init
rules.cases: = R(-1,0,11); the next cycle starts follow from the rules below (abstract run = direct run at 4,200 cycle starts)

rules.name: R1 round
rules.cases: q >= 3, Z has a zero, w = 0 or 2 mod 3; dec: leftmost zero j -> 1, zeros at j-3, j-6, ... >= 2

rules.name: R2 round
rules.cases: q >= 3, Z has a zero, w = 1 mod 3 (one bell pair joins the zone)

rules.name: O2 overflow
rules.cases: q >= 3, w = 2 mod 3: zone + 1 cell, all bits set (v = 2^L - 1)

rules.name: O1 overflow
rules.cases: q >= 3, w = 1 mod 3; allset(u) = every lattice position >= 2 set

rules.name: O0 overflow
rules.cases: q >= 3, w = 0 mod 3: zone + 3 cells, v = 2^L - 2

rules.name: B2 bite
rules.cases: q = 2, zone starts 111; re-parse: a leading 10 of 1Y joins the bell

rules.name: B2' bite, k=1
rules.cases: q = 2, lowest bit set, next clear; Y starts 11

rules.name: H halt
rules.cases: q = 2 and every bit set, k >= 1

rules.name: B1 bite
rules.cases: q = 1, zone 1Y starts 11; re-parse leading 10 of Y; new cycle with n = p+3

rules.name: B0 bite
rules.cases: q = 0, w = 0 mod 3, Z starts 111 (f = 2: n = p+2 and zone 11 Z[3:], 30/30)

rules.name: B2'' nested bite
rules.cases: q = 2, k >= 2 low bits set: an inner wall re-runs rounds on the low part; q' = 5..15, Z' a suffix of Z (top cells sometimes changed). No closed form yet; 49 of 204,953 transitions to 1e9

template.diff: not a near table: architecture match only (mirrored bell + counter + bite)
template.note: Same plan: bell with a moving defect, counter bumped per pass, low-end bite, rare nested eating, halting needs a coincidence; proof via an invariant in progress_nonhalt_cond. Different: counter counts down, bits 3 apart anchored at the far end, defect moves 2 pairs per round, two-level slow counter (v -1 per 2 cycles, level-up at n ~ 2^(L+1)). W4-2's phi/Sweep lemmas do not transfer.

strategy: proof.md on the invariant I: the rules, Lemma M (mod-3 sign law, proved), Lemma K (d >= 2 closure, proved for plain cycles, checked exhaustively), and the entry at step 327. Then Rocq: one lemma per rule, the nested bite by induction on depth, progress_nonhalt_cond over I (W4-2's shape).
risks: Lemma K for cycles with a B2'/B2'' continuation has no paper argument yet; the data show slack (min d' = 5 where 2 is needed).
No halt inside nested levels from K is only checked, not argued.
The Rocq build of the nested bite (a recursion over walls) is the long part.

checkpoint_questions.text: One cycle: do you see the wall step right once per round, the zone at the right edge widen at the overflow, and a bite at the bottom that restarts the wall at the left end?
Counter fill per cycle: does each level read as one smooth descending curve (calm phase), with scattered dots only where a new curve starts (level-up)?

Mechanism validated (rules exact on 99.98% of transitions, abstract run = direct run to 1e11, no halt in ~3e22 steps), but the non-halting invariant and the nested-bite closed form are open. Fund one 2 h stage to hunt both, or park?
